findings.reason: the author should extend the owner (`classify_parked_source` / one shared source-disposition module) with the manifest-facing members and make `_manifest_source_mechanism` and `_classify_export_population` call it, rather than maintain a parallel vocabulary whose divergence the plan is already repairing by hand.
findings.text: the plan builds a per-source disposition vocabulary and classifier in `export.py` (recorded_refusal, refusal_cause_not_recorded, attempt_budget_exhausted, terminal_identity_unusable, identity_not_carried, composition_not_scheduled, waived) while the graph already owns a total, closed per-source disposition classifier with near-identical members at imas_codex/standard_names/graph_ops.py:11405 (`CAP_PARKED_DISPOSITIONS`: name_produced, upstream_quantity_removed, vocabulary_gap, attempt_budget_exhausted, compose_not_applicable, cause_not_recorded) and :11431 (`classify_parked_source`) with its writer :11519 (`record_parked_dispositions`) — the two vocabularies map onto each other (cause_not_recorded↔refusal_cause_not_recorded, attempt_budget_exhausted identical, compose_not_applicable↔composition_not_scheduled, vocabulary_gap↔recorded_refusal) and the plan's §6 defect 4 — the lost-cause sentinel mapped to `composition_not_scheduled`, "its opposite" — is exactly the drift two owners produce; `_has_producing_source` is a second copy of the graph's "name is entailed" predicate (producer edge or live structural child) that `_structural_accept_route` (graph_ops.py:26752) already defines, which the plan verified "against four independent sites" rather than calling one; and the §2 census re-implements the pipeline admission gates by its own admission (eligibility-census.md:41) and reports 140 rows where its vocabulary disagrees with the recorded reason

rubric_items.deep_module: pass — no new module was created; the added behaviour is folded into the export owner behind one interface, `describe_manifest_generability` (imas_codex/standard_names/export.py:2496), which hides the mechanism ladder, the disposition derivation and the carried/uncarried partition. The supporting functions build a ladder (record → `_source_disposition` → `_manifest_source_mechanism` → aggregate), not a spread of parallel wrappers over the same call.
rubric_items.duplicate_owner: a finding — the plan adds a second per-source disposition classifier and a second closed disposition vocabulary inside `export.py`, beside the classifier the graph already owns, and the plan's own §6 defect 4 is the divergence between the two vocabularies.
rubric_items.interface_budget: pass — public_definitions 0, cli_options 0, mcp_views 0, refusal_families 0; every addition in the design is an underscore-private function, an internal reason string, or a data declaration (waived_sources.yaml), none of which adds to the four counted families.
rubric_items.reuse_search: pass — the plan searched the two repositories it names: the export-surface reuse map (docs/evidence/unbound-source-backlog/export-surface-reuse-map.md) and the figure audit record the per-symbol reuse map, and the §6 repairs cite exact file:line reads (export.py:617-640 producer-flag projection; graph_ops.py:26690 structural source_free at :26752 `_structural_accept_route`; graph_ops.py:12893 `fetch_manifest_source_release_rows`), so the producer predicate reuses flags the population query already fetched rather than adding a query.
rubric_items.thin_wrapper: pass — the `manifest_generability` gate (export.py:3517) is not a thin layer over `manifest_source_accounting` (export.py:3488): the plan states in its own text that the accounting gate closes on record count and passes an excluded source, and the new gate carries the per-source mechanism verdict, so it adds a refusal the existing gate cannot express. The waiver declaration is a data file, not a wrapper.
